The immediate scope is only the analytic dimension and finite-pole consumers.

review.scopeProgress: The complete analytic-to-actual-field comparison now compiles. It uses the already reviewed pole-clearing and basis-relation argument, with a natural bound from the native finite-coordinate degree-dimension maximum. A copied standalone constant-germ wrapper was removed before auditing because the generic dimension theorem already uses its own constancy proof; no downstream field-comparison input needed that wrapper.

discharged: Every function meromorphic in the constructed actual complex Kummer cover charts agrees in every punctured chart germ with one element of the literal splitting field. The existing generic compact-manifold results supply analytic dimension and effective pole bounds. The native finite-coordinate degree-dimension maximum supplies finite divisor spaces, a pole-clearing multiplier and two sufficiently large bases. Their faithful residue-germ relation identifies the analytic function as a quotient in the same field. No analytic/algebraic comparison, geometric compactness or connectedness, canonical genus, Riemann-Roch or dimension-bound hypothesis remains.
